issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the total-students accessor: the problem statement text uses the snake_case name `get_total_number_of_students()` (problem_statement.md line 41), while the UML in the same problem statement uses the camelCase `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (problem_statement.md line 70), the template TODO references the camelCase name in Lecture.java (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 12), and the solution implementation defines `public int getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 75). This inconsistency can confuse students about the exact method signature to implement and may lead to mismatches with tests or automatic graders that expect the camelCase name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all materials. Update the problem statement textual description to use the camelCase name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (matching the UML, template TODO, and solution). Verify and update any other occurrences (examples, tests, and comments) to the same camelCase identifier so students implement the correct signature.

issues.description: The problem statement uses a snake_case identifier `get_total_number_of_students()` (problem_statement.md) while the template comments and the solution implement and refer to the Java-style camelCase method `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This mismatch between the problem text and the code artifacts can confuse students about the exact method name they should implement in Java.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier naming consistent by updating the problem statement to use the Java camelCase name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` so it matches the template comments and the solution implementation. This preserves Java naming conventions and reduces student confusion.
